_doc: PROPOSED sector-profile pins for the top Tokyo names (agent, 2026-11-28). NOT ACTIVE: nothing reads this file at run time. A pin makes a name TUNED (src/data/coverage.py -> 'new' instead of 'limited' billing) and fixes its valuation profile, so each one is the owner's decision. To accept a row, copy [sector, profile] into src/data/industry_profile_map.json ticker_overrides (bump its version) and run tests/test_japan_market.py. 'fmp_industry' and 'routes_today' were measured 2026-11-28 (FMP profile + industry_profile_map.profile_for_ticker); 'keep' means the industry row already routes where a practitioner would, and the pin would only mark the name tuned.

7203.T.name: Toyota Motor
7203.T.reason: Auto OEM with a captive finance arm (Toyota Financial Services): the owner's 2026-11-25 auto rule (industrial EV/EBIT ex-captive + captive at P/TBV) applies; note the firm-CAPM beta relevers at captive debt (1.98) until the captive SOTP runs.

7267.T.name: Honda Motor
7267.T.reason: Same as Toyota (captive finance: American Honda Finance).

6758.T.name: Sony Group
6758.T.reason: Games, music, pictures, image sensors, electronics: a segment SOTP is the desk method; the ecosystem profile is the closest single archetype. Sony Financial was spun off (Oct 2025).

6861.T.name: Keyence
6861.T.reason: Factory-automation sensors and measurement instruments sold direct: a capital-goods business (orders follow manufacturing capex), not a software-style platform. Peers SMC/Fanuc route to Capital Goods already.

6954.T.name: Fanuc
6954.T.reason: CNC and robots; net-cash balance sheet (cash-rich rule applies).

7011.T.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
7011.T.reason: Energy systems, defence, aero; long-cycle order book. A defence profile pin is an owner option.

6501.T.name: Hitachi
6501.T.reason: Digital systems (Lumada), energy, mobility, connective industries after a decade of disposals: an operating conglomerate, not a holdco.

8035.T.name: Tokyo Electron
8035.T.reason: Wafer-fab equipment maker (coater/developer, etch, deposition): the AMAT/LRCX archetype, not a chip manufacturer. FMP labels every chip-related name 'Semiconductors'.

6981.T.name: Murata Manufacturing
6981.T.reason: Passive components (MLCC the largest line) and RF modules: a cyclical component manufacturer, not a platform.

4063.T.name: Shin-Etsu Chemical
4063.T.reason: Profit is roughly half silicon wafers / electronic materials and half PVC (Shintech) and silicones. Commodity chemicals undervalues the wafer franchise; electronic materials overstates the PVC half. Owner to choose (or SOTP).

9984.T.name: SoftBank Group
9984.T.reason: An investment holding company (Arm, SoftBank Corp., Vision Funds, OpenAI), valued by the street on NAV less net debt at a discount. Valuing it as a telecom carrier on EV/EBITDA consolidates SoftBank Corp.'s EBITDA and ignores the portfolio. The look-through needs a holdco_sotp template with the stakes from SBG's latest results presentation and an OWNER-SET discount (holdco_discount_not_constant): do not pin until both exist.

8058.T.name: Mitsubishi Corp.
8058.T.reason: Sogo shosha (trading house): equity-method resource and consumer stakes plus trading. Desks price on P/E and P/B vs ROE, with a SOTP cross-check. The JPX 'Conglomerates' comps cohort is dominated by the five trading houses, so the relative legs are effectively a trading-house basket; a dedicated 'Trading House' profile is the cleaner fix (owner).

8306.T.name: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group
8306.T.reason: Megabank; the profile is right but its calibration row is US (P/TBV 2.2x, CoE 9.3%): see docs/markets/JAPAN.md 'Megabank calibration'.

8411.T.name: Mizuho Financial Group
8411.T.reason: FMP labels Mizuho 'Banks - Regional'; it is the third megabank (MUFG/SMFG peer), not a US-style super-regional.

8766.T.name: Tokio Marine
8766.T.reason: P&C insurer; large cross-shareholdings being sold down (announced plan to reduce them to zero; verify timing) -- investment securities matter to book value.

9432.T.name: NTT
9432.T.reason: Integrated carrier (NTT Docomo, NTT Data now 100%).

9983.T.name: Fast Retailing
9983.T.reason: Uniqlo; vertically integrated apparel retail. Large net cash.

6098.T.name: Recruit Holdings
6098.T.reason: Indeed/Glassdoor HR-tech platform plus staffing; the platform profile fits HR Technology (~half of EBITDA).

7974.T.name: Nintendo
7974.T.reason: Same profile the owner pinned EA / TTWO to (Wave 7). Large net cash (verify before use).

4568.T.name: Daiichi Sankyo
4568.T.reason: ADC pipeline (Enhertu): the rNPV add-on matters more than the trailing multiple.

4502.T.name: Takeda Pharmaceutical
4502.T.reason: Global innovative pharma (Entyvio, plasma-derived therapies), not a generics/specialty house.

4661.T.name: Oriental Land
4661.T.reason: Tokyo Disney Resort operator (theme parks + hotels); capex-heavy expansion cycle.

derivation.p_tbv: Megabank P/TBV at the 2026-11-27 close on 30 Sep 2026 book (FMP quarterly balance sheet, equity less goodwill and intangibles; shares = quote market cap / price): MUFG 1.73x, SMFG 1.58x, Mizuho 1.80x -> median 1.73x, mean 1.70x. The JPX 'Banks - Diversified' comps median P/B is 1.13x (includes the trust banks and smaller lenders). The US row's 2.2x priced MUFG's P/TBV leg at ~JP¥4,070 against a JP¥3,192 spot.
derivation.coe: Market-implied from the Gordon P/B identity on MUFG: P/B 1.58 = (ROE 12.4% TTM - g 2.7%, capped at the JGB 10y) / (CoE - g) -> CoE 8.8%. The CAPM at beta 1 on the JGB curve gives 2.70% + 4.41% = 7.1% (no JPY country premium authored), which no Japanese bank desk uses; the US row's 9.3% sits 50bp above the market-implied figure.
derivation.target_roe: Unchanged at 12%: MUFG TTM ROE 12.4% (FMP key-metrics-ttm). The megabanks' own medium-term ROE targets should be confirmed from their plans before acceptance.
